Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the usual vendor deposit, the vendor payment terms, the days to warn that a document expires and the days after which a vendor counts as dormant.
Check Vendors, Venues and Events. Vendor and venue details come with the demo; replace them with your own. Categories missing and vendors booked fill in from the bookings.
Enter every booking on Vendor Bookings with the quoted and agreed price, the deposit share and the balance date. The deposit, the balance and the days to the balance date fill in.
Enter every payment on Vendor Payments. Days late, the open amount and the payment check fill in, and Payment Calendar shows what must go out in the next 13 weeks.
Use Quote Requests to compare vendors and Availability Holds to keep track of dates held. The saving against the other quotes and the days left on a hold fill in.
Record scores on Vendor Scorecards after each event and calls on Vendor Contact Log. The average score of every vendor shows on Vendors.
Keep Vendor Documents and Vendor Onboarding up to date, so you know which vendors have valid insurance and which onboarding is not finished.
When a vendor cancels, enter it on Cancellations and use Cost to Replace a Vendor. Preferred Vendors gives the first and second choice for the category.
Enter disputed invoices on Disputed Invoices and use the Dispute Credit calculator to work out the credit to ask for.
Use Venue Load-in Rules, Rental Inventory, Referral Fees and Vendor Price Changes for the details that save a phone call on the day.

Use the 14 calculators before you decide: dates, replacement, payment priority, quotes, spend share, deposits at risk, overtime, referral fee, lead time, reliability, cash for four weeks, meals, dispute credit and the catering grid.
Read Vendors Dashboard and Charts every week: payments due, overdue vendor amount, committed cost, deposits, holds and documents.

Guest groups by event with their replies
One row per event and guest group with the guests invited and the answers; the guests not yet answered, the response share and the yes share fill in by themselves.
Plus-ones and children with their meals
One row per plus-one or child with the guest they come with, their meal and whether they need a seat; the guest name and the child meal flag fill in by themselves.
One row per gift received with the date and the day the thank-you note went out; the days to thank, the sent or overdue check and the guest name fill in by themselves.
Shuttle manifest with seats per run
One row per guest who needs a shuttle with the pickup point, the pickup time and the return time; the guest name, the seats booked on the same run and the vehicles needed fill in by themselves.
One row per guest in the room block with the room type, the nights, the rate and whether the room is booked; the guest name, the total cost and the closing date of the block fill in by themselves.
VIPs and speakers with arrival and slot
One row per VIP or speaker with the role, the arrival time, the minutes on stage and the seat; the end of the slot fills in by itself.
One row per guest of a completed event with the arrival window, the table and the meal served; the guest name and the on time, late or no-show check fill in by themselves.
RSVP reminders and the answers they brought
One row per reminder sent to a guest with the channel and the answer so far; the guest name, the phone, the days to answer and the reply check fill in by themselves.
Name and place cards with the printing check
One row per name or place card with its text and whether it is printed and placed; the guest name and the ready flag fill in by themselves.
Final head count sheet with the cost of empty seats
One row per event with the count given to the caterer and to the venue, the seats booked and the guests who came; the gap, the empty seats, their cost and the lock check fill in by themselves.
